title: ALMA and VLA measurements of frequency-dependent time lags in Sagittarius A*: evidence for a relativistic outflow
question: Do Sgr A* light curves at 19-100 GHz show frequency-dependent time lags indicating an expanding, relativistic outflow/jet?

data.bands: ALMA bands 3, 6, 7 observed; only ~100 GHz (Band 3) used here

what.value: Size-frequency relation of Sgr A*: 0.52 mas x (lambda/cm)^1.3

evidence.quote: we can use the size-frequency relation of Sgr A* as presented in (cite: Falcke09) as additional information

what.value: Miyazaki 102-90 GHz time delay of -2.56 ± 0.9 min

evidence.quote: they reported the time delay between 102 GHz and 90 GHz as being $-2.56 \pm 0.9$ min

recipe.method: Average unflagged visibilities per scan over baselines >150 klambda; errors from visibility amplitude spread
ZDCF; zero-lag spikes dominate so no lags derived
FRED fit to bump (7-11h UT VLA, 6:50-8:50 UT ALMA); Monte Carlo dropping half of VLA points, 500 iterations
assumptions: ALMA bump is same event as VLA maxima

recipe.method: Combine linear lag vs wavelength fit with size-frequency relation and light-travel-time lag formula for inclination
assumptions: Distance 8.3 kpc; one-sided jet at i=90 deg or two-sided jet

evidence.quote: we obtain $\alpha = 0.50 \pm 0.07$ when only the VLA data are used

answer_key.quantity: Time of maximum at 19 GHz (all data)

evidence.quote: we detect a time lag of 28 $\pm$ 9 minutes between these two frequencies
predicts a time lag between these frequencies of $1.7 \pm 0.6$ min
our data suggest an outflow velocity of $\sim$0.77$c$ ($\gamma\beta\approx1.2$)
indicates a minimum flow velocity of $v_f = 0.5$c ($\gamma\beta=0.58$) for an inclination of 60$^\circ$

not_stated_but_needed: ALMA CASA version and exact QA2 script
FRED fit initial guesses and weighting
Numerical time lag versus wavelength fit coefficients
missing_for_reproduction: FRED fitting details and starting values
score_reason: Public data and simple method, but custom calibration and fit details are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, simple visibility-based light curves and FRED fits with numeric results in Table 1.
